title: French grammar
intro: A working reference for beginners to intermediate learners. Every pattern comes with real sentences and a translation: read a section, notice the shape, then listen for it in what you watch and read.

sections.title: Nouns, articles & gender
sections.text: Every noun is masculine or feminine; learn it with its article. Endings help: **-tion, -sion, -té, -ure, -ette** are usually feminine (la nation, la liberté); **-ment, -age, -eau, -isme** usually masculine (le moment, le fromage). The plural **-s** is usually silent, so listen to the article: **le/la** vs **les**. **à + le = au**, **à + les = aux**, **de + le = du**, **de + les = des**.

head: Definite
Indefinite
rows: l'ami, l'école | the friend, the school
les livres, les tables | the books, the tables

examples.translation: The price of bread is going up.

sections.title: Some, any & none (du, de la, des)
sections.text: French needs an article where English often has none: **Je mange du pain.** After a negation, and after quantities (**beaucoup de, un peu de, un kilo de**), it becomes plain **de**. Verbs of liking take the definite article: **J'aime le café** (coffee in general).

examples.text: Il y a beaucoup de monde.
examples.translation: There are a lot of people.

sections.title: Subject pronouns, tu & vous, on
sections.text: In conversation **on** usually replaces nous: **On y va ?** (Shall we go?). It takes the il/elle verb form. **vous** is both polite singular and plural; when in doubt with an adult you don't know, use vous.

examples.text: Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?

sections.title: Present tense (regular verbs)
sections.rule: Drop -er, -ir or -re and add the ending; most -er endings sound the same.
sections.text: Nine out of ten verbs end in **-er**, and in speech je parle, tu parles, il parle and ils parlent all sound identical. The present also means "I am doing": **Je lis** = I read / I'm reading. To stress "right now", use **être en train de + infinitive**.

examples.text: Les cours finissent à cinq heures.
Je suis en train de cuisiner.

sections.title: Key irregular verbs
sections.text: Also very common: **pouvoir** (je peux, ils peuvent), **vouloir** (je veux, ils veulent), **devoir** (je dois), **venir** (je viens, ils viennent), **prendre** (je prends, nous prenons, ils prennent). Age and many feelings use avoir: **j'ai vingt ans, j'ai faim, j'ai froid**.

examples.translation: Do you want to come with us?

sections.title: Negation (ne … pas and friends)
sections.text: The two parts wrap the conjugated verb (**Je ne parle pas**) and the auxiliary in compound tenses (**Je n'ai pas compris**). In everyday speech the **ne** is often dropped: **Je sais pas**, **C'est pas grave**. Listen for **pas**, **jamais**, **rien** to catch a negation.

head: Pattern
Example
rows: Je ne sais pas. | I don't know.
Il ne mange jamais de viande. | He never eats meat.
Je ne vois rien. | I can't see anything.
Il n'y a personne. | There's nobody.
Elle ne fume plus. | She doesn't smoke any more.

sections.title: Asking questions
sections.text: **quel / quelle / quels / quelles** (which, what) agrees with its noun: **Quelle heure est-il ?** In speech the question word often comes last: **Tu vas où ?** **C'est combien ?**

head: Style
Example
rows: Tu viens ce soir ? | Are you coming tonight?
Est-ce que tu viens ce soir ?
où | where ;; quand | when ;; comment | how ;; pourquoi | why ;; combien | how much ;; qui | who ;; quoi / que | what

examples.text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais ce week-end ?
examples.translation: What are you doing this weekend?

examples.note: question word at the end: spoken

sections.title: Adjectives & agreement
sections.text: Adjectives agree with the noun and usually come **after** it: **une voiture rouge**. A short group comes before: **beau, bon, grand, petit, jeune, vieux, nouveau, joli, mauvais** (BAGS: beauty, age, goodness, size). Before a masculine vowel: **un bel appartement, un nouvel ami, un vieil homme**.

sections.title: Passé composé (what happened)
sections.rule: avoir or être in the present + past participle (-er → -é, -ir → -i, -re → -u).
sections.text: Most verbs use **avoir**. About fifteen verbs of movement or change of state use **être** (aller, venir, arriver, partir, entrer, sortir, monter, descendre, naître, mourir, rester, tomber, devenir, retourner), and so do all reflexive verbs (**je me suis levé**). With être the participle agrees: **elle est partie, ils sont venus**. Irregular participles: **fait, dit, pris, mis, vu, eu, été, pu, voulu, lu, écrit**.

examples.text: Nous nous sommes promenés au bord de la mer.
examples.translation: We went for a walk by the sea.

sections.title: Imparfait vs. passé composé
sections.text: Think of a film: the imparfait sets the scene, the passé composé moves the story. Only **être** is irregular in the imparfait (**j'étais**). Signal words: **souvent, tous les jours, d'habitude** → imparfait; **soudain, un jour, ensuite** → passé composé.

head: imparfait
passé composé
rows: background, description, habits, states: what was going on
events, completed actions: what happened next
Il pleuvait. | It was raining. ;; Quand j'étais petit… | When I was little…
Le téléphone a sonné. | The phone rang. ;; J'ai ouvert la porte. | I opened the door.

examples.text: Je lisais quand tu as appelé.
examples.translation: I was reading when you called.

examples.text: Le dimanche, on allait chez ma grand-mère.
examples.translation: On Sundays we used to go to my grandmother's.

examples.text: Il faisait froid, alors j'ai mis un manteau.
examples.translation: It was cold, so I put on a coat.

sections.title: Object pronouns, y & en
sections.text: Pronouns go **before the conjugated verb**: **Je le vois. Je lui parle.** With an infinitive they go before the infinitive: **Je vais le faire.** In positive commands they follow with a hyphen: **Dis-le !** **y** replaces à + place or thing (**J'y vais**); **en** replaces de + noun or a quantity (**J'en veux deux**).

head: Direct (whom / what)
Indirect (to whom)
rows: en | some, of it, from there

examples.text: Tu connais Marie ? Oui, je la connais.
examples.translation: Do you know Marie? Yes, I know her.

examples.text: Je lui ai envoyé un message.
examples.translation: I sent him / her a message.

examples.text: Des pommes ? J'en achète un kilo.
examples.translation: Apples? I'll buy a kilo (of them).

sections.title: Reflexive verbs
sections.text: Many daily-routine verbs are reflexive: **se réveiller, se laver, s'habiller, se coucher**, and **s'appeler** (Je m'appelle…). Some mean "each other": **Ils se parlent tous les jours.** In the passé composé they take être.

examples.text: Je me lève à sept heures.
Elles se sont rencontrées à Paris.

sections.title: The future (aller + infinitive, futur simple)
sections.text: In speech the **futur proche** is the everyday future. The futur simple is common in writing, plans that are further off, and after **quand** about the future: **Quand j'aurai le temps, je t'appellerai.**

head: futur proche
futur simple
rows: Je vais partir. | I'm going to leave.
être → ser- ;; avoir → aur- ;; aller → ir- ;; faire → fer- ;; pouvoir → pourr- ;; venir → viendr- ;; voir → verr-

examples.text: On va manger au restaurant ce soir.
examples.translation: We're going to eat out tonight.

examples.text: Quand tu seras à Paris, appelle-moi.
examples.translation: When you're in Paris, call me.

sections.title: Conditional & si clauses
sections.text: Never put the conditional or the future after **si** meaning "if": **Si j'avais** (not si j'aurais). The conditional also makes requests polite: **Je voudrais un café. Pourriez-vous m'aider ?**

head: Situation
si-clause
main clause
rows: Si tu viens, | If you come,
on ira au cinéma. | we'll go to the cinema.
Si j'avais le temps, | If I had time,
Si j'avais su, | If I had known,
je serais venu. | I would have come.

examples.translation: I'd like to book a table.

examples.text: Si j'étais toi, je lui parlerais.
examples.translation: If I were you, I'd talk to him.

sections.title: The subjunctive
sections.rule: ils-form of the present, drop -ent, add -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent (ils parlent → que je parl{e}).
sections.text: The subjunctive follows **que** after necessity, wishes, feelings and doubt, when the two clauses have different subjects (same subject: infinitive, **Je veux partir**). Irregular: **être → que je sois, avoir → que j'aie, faire → que je fasse, aller → que j'aille, pouvoir → que je puisse, savoir → que je sache**.

head: Trigger
Example
rows: Il faut que tu viennes. | You have to come.
Je veux qu'il parte. | I want him to leave.
Je suis content que tu sois là. | I'm glad you're here.
Je doute qu'il ait raison. | I doubt he's right.
bien que, pour que, avant que, à moins que

examples.text: Il faut que je parte maintenant.
Bien qu'il soit fatigué, il continue.
examples.translation: Although he's tired, he keeps going.

examples.text: Je préfère que tu me le dises.

sections.title: Relative pronouns (qui, que, où, dont)
sections.text: English can drop "that"; French never drops **que**. Choose qui if the next word is a verb (the noun is the subject), que if a new subject follows.

head: Pronoun
Role
Example
rows: l'homme qui parle | the man who is talking
le livre que je lis | the book (that) I'm reading
la ville où j'habite ;; le jour où je l'ai vu
le film dont je t'ai parlé | the film I told you about
Ce que tu dis est vrai. | What you say is true.

examples.text: C'est la femme qui habite à côté.
examples.translation: That's the woman who lives next door.

examples.text: Le café où on se voit est fermé.
examples.translation: The café where we meet is closed.

sections.title: Comparing
sections.text: **meilleur** is the adjective (better wine), **mieux** the adverb (sings better). With nouns use **plus de / moins de / autant de**: **Il a plus de temps que moi.**

head: Pattern
Example
rows: Paris est plus grand que Lyon.
Il est aussi grand que moi.
Ce vin est meilleur. ;; Elle chante mieux.

examples.text: Le train est plus rapide que le bus.
examples.translation: The train is faster than the bus.

examples.text: C'est le meilleur restaurant du quartier.
examples.translation: It's the best restaurant in the area.

sections.title: One-page memory map
points: Learn le or la with every noun; plural -s is silent, so listen to the article.
du / de la / des for 'some'; after a negation or a quantity it's just de.
on is the everyday 'we'; vous is polite or plural.
Negation wraps the verb: ne … pas; in speech the ne often disappears.
Passé composé tells what happened; imparfait paints the background.
être verbs (movement, reflexive) agree in the passé composé: elle est partie.
aller + infinitive is the everyday future.
Object pronouns, y and en go before the conjugated verb.
Never the conditional after si: si j'avais…, je ferais…
The subjunctive follows que after il faut, wishes, feelings and doubt.
sections.tip: Listening strategy: French runs words together (liaison: les_amis, on_a). When a sentence blurs, listen for the subject pronoun and the article first: they tell you who and how many, even when the verb ending is silent.
